Non-linear gradient interpolation is a technique for pre-integrated direct volume rendering that reduces shading errors by interpolating gradients between front and back samples along a quadratic curve instead of a linear segment, allowing accurate computation of 2D pre-integration look-up tables [S1].

It explains that this approach reduces shading errors (specifically loss of luminous energy) and allows for the computation of 2D pre-integration look-up tables, avoiding the impracticality of higher-dimensional tables required for accurate front/back normal consideration.
